newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China unruffled by legislature boycotts-Qian.
newsitem.headline: China unruffled by legislature boycotts-Qian.

text.p: China appeared on Tuesday to be unruffled by the row over the swearing in of Hong Kong's provisional legislature, which is being boycotted by the United States and Britain.

U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and new British Prime Minister Tony Blair have said they will not attend the inauguration of the legislature, hand-picked by Beijing for the June 30 handover of the British colony.

Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen, interviewed by Hong Kong's South China Morning Post in Beijing, said: "We naturally welcome and would like to invite those representatives who have already attended the handover ceremony to attend the inauguration for the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
"It is their own business as to whether they attend or not."
Qian said he was hoping for a new start in Sino-British relations after Labour's landslide election victory last month.
"Hong Kong's return happens to be the first quite important event facing the new British government and I am confident Hong Kong will have a smooth transition."
He acknowledged there was some dissent in Hong Kong in the lead-up to the handover but said it came from a tiny minority.
"Hong Kong has a population of 6.3 million or 6.5 million and, judging from the celebrations they are having to mark the return, most people are very happy about this event.
"Even if some people are not for this, they are a small number, less than one percent of the total population."
